title: UPDATE: Apple Plans Next-Gen Touchscreen MacBooks With M7 Chips and New AI Hardware
summary:
Apple is developing an updated line of touch-screen MacBook Pros for next year that will feature M7 Pro and M7 Max chips, according to Mark Gurman. The next-generation laptops will include specialized hardware to enhance artificial intelligence capabilities and will add a new entry-level 14 inch model featuring the thinner chassis and slimmer bezels found on the high-end configurations.

The planned expansion follows the company's recent introduction of the first touch-enabled MacBooks, which start at $2,899 for the 14 inch and $3,399 for the 16 inch versions. The move to include touch interfaces marks a departure from a long-held corporate philosophy that dismissed the technology as impractical for laptops due to arm fatigue and ergonomics.

// Will be interesting to see how this "modality" functions. 

In general modes have a tricky problem where having a manual switch is something tech enthusiasts like (like a convertible car or unfolding phone) but humans in daily use rarely want to put this much thought into using something or find it inconvenient. 

OTOH, automagically switching modes when there is a cost and complexity to switching wrong means that the pick will be wrong some percentage > 0% and that means it will feel like it is wrong all the time.

In Windows 8 we were criticized for having two modes but there was no switch and touch worked as well as we could make it work with legacy apps in a desktop environment. There were APIs and design guidelines that could be followed. For new apps the APIs just worked mouse or touch. Later in Windows 8.x and up there was a "touch mode" which only proved to be wrong most of the time and no one managed it manually. 

Today's Mac generally relies on very little third party software and Apple can make all their "desktop" work fine with touch. There are utilities and some third parties used a good amount (Office, Adobe) but the long tail isn't as present on Mac OS (nor has it been for a very long time). And the vast majority of tech enthusiasts in the Apple world today are CLI people, not sitting in Win32 native apps like they were during the toaster-refrigerator era. So we'll see how this one aspect plays out.

I, for one, look forward to having touch work on stuff like browsing since to this day I still touch the screen by accident. As I said in 2012 -- Once you touch your screen you won't ever go back. https://t.co/cVTmVksy2Y
